title: Communication-Free Multi-Agent Control under Local Temporal Tasks and Relative-Distance Constraints
review_status: full-text audit complete; theorem and simulation evidence checked; explicit point-agent/no-collision and connected-initial-graph assumptions recorded
sections_checked: §4.3 hybrid switching protocol and task-satisfaction theorem
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2014-10-31; no venue publication verified in sampled metadata
evidence_note: Formal guarantee for local LTL satisfaction and relative-distance maintenance under the proposed controller, with computer simulations. Assumes 2D single-integrator point masses (collisions not modeled), common sensing radius, initially connected graph, and separated task regions; not a physical collision-safety validation.

title: Evoplex: A platform for agent-based modeling on networks
review_status: full-text audit complete; software contribution distinguished from evidence about agent-task outcomes
evidence_note: Presents a graph-based agent simulation platform and multithreaded experiment workflow. The illustrative 99×99 prisoner’s-dilemma experiment uses a single trial; this demonstrates the software, not a replicated behavioral finding or comparative proof of better agent coordination.

title: Collision Detection for Agents in Multi-Agent Pathfinding
review_status: full-text audit complete; analytical taxonomy, error consequences, modeled motion scope, and future-work boundary checked
sections_checked: §2 collision detection taxonomy and false positive/negative consequences
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 dated 2019-11-15; technical report; no venue publication verified
evidence_note: Technical report categorizing collision-detection approaches and deriving exact intervals for specified shapes/motion. Coarse geometric containers may yield false positives; sparse sampling may yield false negatives. Exact unsafe intervals for accelerating agents are left as future work; not a broad deployment evaluation.

title: Energy Management of Multi-mode Hybrid Electric Vehicles based on Hand-shaking Multi-agent Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; quantitative comparison checked and bounded to MATLAB/Simulink software-in-the-loop evidence
sections_checked: §4 MATLAB/Simulink software-in-the-loop setup and driving cycles
§4 results across three initial battery states
evidence_note: With independence ratio 0.2, the two-agent DDPG system reports 2.13%, 2.538%, and 2.554% fuel savings across three initial SoC settings and lower SoC error than the single-agent baseline. Evidence is simulation on a constructed cycle assembled from four standard cycles, not road testing; authors warn ratio tuning is required and poor settings can destabilize joint learning.

title: A Large Language Model-based multi-agent manufacturing system for intelligent shopfloor
review_status: full-text audit complete; physical shopfloor results, protocol sensitivity, model variation, API errors, human fallback, and data-security assumptions checked
sections_checked: §3 physical shopfloor architecture and API/security assumptions
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2024-05-28; venue year not verified in this audit
evidence_note: On the reported shopfloor, Hunyuan with reference answers achieves makespans 583/609/633 s for FIFO/FILO/SPT, versus Random 690/743/714; without reference answers it degrades to 990/993/1022 s. Five repetitions; 11 erroneous outputs in 49,437 API calls (mostly network errors with retries). Ambiguous decisions can be referred to a human; external closed-source API use is explicitly conditioned on low data-security requirements. Results are specific to system, prompt/reference protocol, models, and shopfloor.

title: S5-SHB Agent: Society 5.0 Enabled Multi-Model Agentic Blockchain Framework for Smart Home
review_status: full-text audit complete; evaluation is simulated, decision acceptance separated from correctness/safety, latency/throughput tradeoff and internal figures inconsistency noted
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2026-03-23; preprint, not peer-reviewed per paper
evidence_note: Eight sessions (four Gemini variants × two conditions) over 30 cycles in a simulated 16-device household; fixed injected-threat schedule. Authors report 3,916 accepted decisions, but acceptance is not ground-truth correctness or safe physical actuation. Limitations include simulation-only evaluation, one LLM provider, fixed threats, one household. Balanced vs aggressive adaptive blockchain reports 15.2 vs 5.4 ms emergency response in table, while the discussion gives 6.8 vs 3.0 ms; overall latency/throughput also trade off (478 ms/15.9 tx/s vs 4642 ms/1.5 tx/s).

title: SimuHome: A Temporal- and Environment-Aware Benchmark for Smart Home LLM Agents
review_status: full-text citation follow-up audit complete; simulator state outcomes and feedback recovery checked; not physical-home validation
sections_checked: §5 evaluation and results across query types
evidence_note: Manually validated 600-episode benchmark; version 3 evaluates 18 LLMs. Final home state verifies executable tasks. Explicit control recovers from initial invalid tool calls in over 40% of successful QT3 episodes, while workflow scheduling remains the hardest case and self-correction is weak. Simulator-grounded, not a real-home longitudinal trial.

title: SMH-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Environment-Grounded Reasoning and Action in Smart Homes
review_status: full-text citation follow-up audit complete; environment-state evaluation, scale/complexity results, and reproducibility status checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2026-06-01; benchmark paper states data/code forthcoming
evidence_note: HomeEnv executes agent operations and verifies resulting state transitions. The benchmark contains 1,100 human-audited tasks over 7 categories/22 subcategories and simulated homes up to 135 devices; 13 LLMs are evaluated. Strong performance on simple/explicit tasks coexists with inconsistency and weakness on complex homes, ambiguity, automation, and personalization. This improves outcome measurement but remains simulator evidence; data/code are listed as forthcoming in the audited version.

title: Evil-AI Benchmark: An Evaluation Framework for Adversarial Security Assessment of LLM Agents in Smart Environments
review_status: citation follow-up abstract/peer-reviewed publication record checked; full-text PDF access returned HTTP 403, therefore not counted as full-text audited
sections_checked: publisher/institution research-portal abstract and reported evaluation protocol
evidence_note: Abstract reports five threat types, 350 scenarios across five smart-environment domains, eight LLMs, dual-model scoring plus human verification, and an Arduino-driven servo for physical verification of actuator-trigger events. Attack rates vary 0.8%-54%. This is component-level physical verification, not evidence of an entire household system's end-to-end safety. Full text remains unaudited because PDF download was denied (HTTP 403).
